insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's receipt-verified GMV hit $196,247 across 4,249 confirmed transactions in 14 days — each receipt is a cryptographic proof of purchase, not an inferred intent signal. Brands paying $5+ CPM for probabilistic audience targeting are funding inference where deterministic purchase proof now exists at scale.

Grocery and supermarket receipts account for 29% of 14-day volume (1,230 receipts / $54,190), making it the single largest category by transaction count — a reliable, recurring signal pool for CPG and grocery-adjacent brands seeking verified purchase audiences.

insights.topic: Unknown category: elevated ticket size signals premium or specialty spend
insights.insight: The 'Unknown' category carries an average ticket of $92.43 versus $44.06 for grocery — more than double — and represents 342 receipts and $31,610 in 14-day GMV. For brands targeting higher-spend consumers, this unclassified segment warrants investigation as a potential premium or specialty retail signal.

Category entropy reached 2.908 bits at the most recent reading, with restaurants and dining becoming newly visible in the 14-day aggregate — meaning the verified purchase pool is broadening beyond grocery into food service, retail, and fuel. Brands outside CPG now have a credible entry point for cookieless, receipt-verified targeting.

insights.topic: Geographic expansion is organic and ongoing
insights.insight: Active coverage has reached 19 metro areas across 30 category/metro signal cells, with new CBSAs appearing individually rather than in bursts — the pattern of organic diffusion, not bulk onboarding. For brands planning regional or geo-targeted campaigns, the addressable footprint is expanding incrementally and verifiably.

insights.topic: Cycle ceiling trend: verified GMV peaks are rising
insights.insight: The 7-day GMV cycle high reached $91,361 on November 19, surpassing the prior record of $89,635 set just one day earlier — two consecutive record peaks confirm the ceiling is trending upward. Brands evaluating this data source should note that the verified transaction pool is growing in peak capacity, though floor behavior after UTC rolloffs remains volatile and should be weighted accordingly.
